title: Tilt? Acceleration-Time Graphs Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A bus pulls away, a lift starts to rise, a swing turns back. You feel a push each time, but at a steady speed, even a fast one, you feel nothing. Aarav's water bottle shows it too: the water tilts when he speeds up or brakes, and stays flat when he cruises. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 2, Motion in a Straight Line) we learn to read an acceleration-time graph.

We replay Aarav's ride with the water bottle while his a-t graph draws live: uniform acceleration is a flat line, a change in acceleration is a jump. We build the a-t graph from the slope of the v-t graph, show step by step why the area under an a-t graph is the change in velocity (+6 then -6, back to rest), and draw the famous graph for a ball thrown straight up (a = -9.8 m/s^2 the whole flight, even at the top). Then a worked example, the exam trap about the starting velocity, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Why you feel the push, not the speed
0:27 What is an acceleration-time graph?
0:48 Live ride: the water bottle and the a-t graph
1:26 From the velocity-time graph, step by step
1:54 Flat line: v-t vs a-t + pause and think
2:28 Area = change in velocity
3:11 Ball thrown up + pause and think
3:46 Worked example: the scooter
4:19 Exam trap: area is not the final velocity
4:43 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)

Next episode: Slope and Area Interpretation of Motion Graphs. One graph, two secret tools: how to read any motion graph in seconds.
